title: Assessing Protein Crystal Tolerance of Chemistry Reagents for HT-Crystallographic Screening
author: Milo Cooper
materials: Prepare a plate containing the reagents and crude reactions to be tested by pipetting the reagents and reactions into a 384-well PP plate. If the controls plate has already been prepared, skip forwards to Step 4. Refer to “control-plate-map.csv” for the plate map format. Prepare 100 µL 500 millimolar (mM) stock solutions of the reagents and catalysts in DMSO. Halve the concentration to 250 millimolar (mM) if there are solubility issues. Transfer 50 µL of the of the stock solutions prepared to a 384-PP Echo compatible control plate. If available, transfer 50 µL of representative crude reaction mixtures to the 384-PP control plate. For all solvents that will be used in potential reactions and the DMSO used for the dilutions, add 50 µL of 2% v/v reaction solvent in DMSO to the 384-PP plate.

Assess the data, and tag reagents as “failed” in red, or “suspicious” in orange, according to the standards below. For all failure modes, determine if reagent is critical, or if more viable alternatives exist for the same reaction and role. Check that the DMSO-only controls have survived and do not reach any failure modes. What we define as a “failure”: Type of failure modes and cutoffs: a. Can’t be mounted (2x - 3x for 3 repeats) b. No diffraction (for any repeat) c. Resolution poor (3.0+ Å average) d. Model building failure (Any of: Failed DIMPLE run; Rfree > 0.40; Rcryst > 0.35, occurring 2x – 3x for 3 repeats) What we define as “suspicious” or a partial failure: Partial failure modes and cutoffs: a. Can’t be mounted (1x for 3 repeats) b. N/A c. Resolution poor (2.2 - 3.0 Å average) d. Model building failure (Any of: Failed DIMPLE run; Rfree > 0.40; Rcryst > 0.35, occurring 1x for 3 repeats)

steps.title: Prepare crystallisation plate
steps.instruction: Set up a SwissSci 3‑drop crystallisation plate following the specific crystallisation protocol and incubate the plate in a Formulatrix imager.

steps.title: Grow and image crystals
steps.instruction: Allow crystals to grow to a size suitable for mounting, then image the plates and export a CSV of the targeted drops containing crystals using the CHiMP dispensing file generator on ISPyB.

steps.title: Determine DMSO tolerance
steps.instruction: Perform a solvent‑tolerance test by transferring a dilution series of DMSO (e.g., 25 %, 20 %, 15 %, 10 %, 5 % of the drop volume) into the crystal drops, and assess the maximum % DMSO and soak time the crystals can tolerate.

steps.title: Soak control plate
steps.instruction: Soak a control plate in triplicate using the % DMSO and soak time identified in step 3; include 3× DMSO‑only wells as negative controls and, if available, a known fragment binder as a positive control.

steps.title: Mount crystals at time points
steps.instruction: At 1 h, 2 h, and 3 h after soaking, mount the crystals, cryo‑cool them with the Crystal Shifter, and store them in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Collect diffraction data
steps.instruction: Collect diffraction data from the cryo‑cooled crystals; process the data automatically using Diamond Light Source pipelines (xia2_dials, fast_dp, autoPROC, xia2_3dii, autoPROC + STARANISO) and perform model building with DIMPLE, confirming resolution better than 2.5 Å and successful model building.

steps.title: Load data into XChem Explorer
steps.instruction: Load the ISPyB visit containing the data collection into XChem Explorer (XCE).

steps.title: Run DIMPLE and export results
steps.instruction: Run a DIMPLE automated model‑building job through XCE; when complete, export the XCE results as a CSV file.

steps.title: Visualise results in XtalControl
steps.instruction: Load the ISPyB sample data and the exported XCE CSV into XtalControl for processing and visualisation of each reagent’s outcome.

steps.title: Perform follow‑up soaks if needed
steps.instruction: If any reagent shows failure or partial failure, set up follow‑up soaks with reduced transfer percentages (by thirds or quarters) in a stepped dilution (e.g., start 20 % → 15 % → 10 % → 5 %); perform each dilution in triplicate, ensure transferred volume ≥ 2.5 µL (Echo minimum), and include DMSO‑only controls for each transfer level.

steps.title: Collect and process follow‑up data
steps.instruction: Collect and process diffraction data from the follow‑up soaked crystals using the same pipelines as in step 6.

steps.title: Time‑series follow‑up if still failing
steps.instruction: If failures persist at the lowest transfer percentage, perform a time‑series follow‑up by reducing soak time in 30‑minute increments (00:30:00) and repeat in triplicate.

steps.title: Cryo‑cool after follow‑up
steps.instruction: After each follow‑up soak reaches its designated time, mount and cryo‑cool the crystals with the Crystal Shifter, store in liquid nitrogen, wear appropriate PPE, and use the Crystal Shifter UI to record any observations such as reagent precipitation.

steps.title: Analyze follow‑up diffraction data
steps.instruction: Analyse the diffraction data from follow‑up soaks; XtalControl will separate results by transfer percentage and reagent, allowing batch processing. Return to step 10 if further optimisation is required.
